relevance_note: Patient 1 is an individual with arterial tortuosity syndrome: 'He was diagnosed with ATS after the SLC2A10 gene defect was found.'
method_note: Ophthalmology case series of two patients; written by hand (small Python helper only assembled the JSON). In scope: Patient 1 (ATS, SLC2A10 gene defect; no variant description printed, so variant_original_string = 'not reported') and his two distant cousins said to carry 'the same genetic defect' (no other individual-level detail; labelled 'distant cousin of Patient 1' and 'distant cousin of Patient 1 2'). Patient 2 (working diagnosis EDS musculocontractural type; VUS in COL5A1 and ZNF469, two DCHS1 variants; no SLC2A10 variant or ATS diagnosis) is out of scope and gets no rows; counted in cohort_size_as_stated = 2. n_patients_reported left null because the authors never state a count of SLC2A10 carriers. Patient 1's age (21-year-old) is his age at first presentation to the authors, followed by a 3-year follow-up, so it was not recorded as age at last evaluation (no age at final follow-up is stated). Onset of corneal ectasia/astigmatism at age 11 years recorded on the feature rows, not as disease onset. 'The rest of the anterior exam and dilated fundus exam were within normal limits' is a normal examination as a whole and was recorded as written (excluded) without excluding anything more specific. No checklist feature is addressed for any in-scope person; all checklist items are 'not reported'. Patient 1 is not called proband/index case and this is not a single-patient case report, so is_proband left null. Minor inconsistency in the paper about Patient 2 only (pseudopterygium 25% in figure legend vs 50% in abstract at later follow-up), not extracted.
